# Results — Study 453 (Three-Inside-Up / Down)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **the
three-inside-up flips the trend: a down candle, an inside harami, then a confirming candle that
closes back past the first bar marks a bullish reversal** — encoded as a mechanical rule. Bars
A/B/C are read on closed bars; the signal is complete on the close of the confirming bar *t*; a
long is entered at the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the forward
5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) OHLC for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **64** mechanical confirmed three-inside-up signals pooled across the 5 tapes (trend lookback = 5) |
| Timing / costs | pattern read on the confirming bar's close; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per signal |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument pattern study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — confirmed three-inside-up vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch confirmed-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = confirmed − random.

| horizon | n | confirmed | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (conf−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 64 | +30.4 bps | 61% | +1.22 | +10.3 bps | **+20.1 bps** | +28.4 bps | +0.63 | 0.528 |
| 10-day | 64 | +10.3 bps | 62% | +0.25 | +53.6 bps | **−43.2 bps** | +8.3 bps  | −0.86 | 0.392 |
| 20-day | 64 | −106.9 bps | 47% | −1.61 | +33.1 bps | **−139.9 bps** | −108.9 bps | −1.75 | 0.083 |
| 60-day | 64 | −13.3 bps | 48% | −0.12 | +118.9 bps | **−132.3 bps** | −15.3 bps | −1.04 | 0.302 |

Read it carefully. Unlike the drift-fed dip-buy rules elsewhere on the desk, the confirmed
three-inside-up does not even produce an impressive one-sample *t* — it never clears 2 and turns
**negative** at 20 days (the "bullish reversal" is, on average, followed by a *fall*). Against the
drift-matched random baseline it is **worse at 10/20/60 days** (Δ = −43.2 / −139.9 / −132.3 bps);
the only positive horizon (5-day, +20.1 bps) carries a Welch *t* of just +0.63. The
confirmed-minus-random difference **never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar**. The pattern does not
forecast a reversal.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — the confirmed entry loses to random everywhere

| ticker | entries | confirmed | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (conf−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 11 | −177.4 bps | −1.08 | +39.3 bps | **−216.7 bps** |
| QQQ | 14 | −136.3 bps | −0.62 | +88.2 bps | **−224.5 bps** |
| IWM | 18 | −107.6 bps | −1.21 | +2.7 bps  | **−110.3 bps** |
| DIA | 11 | −93.3 bps  | −0.97 | +33.7 bps | **−127.0 bps** |
| GLD | 10 | −1.6 bps   | −0.01 | +1.5 bps  | **−3.1 bps** |

The confirmed three-inside-up underperforms a random-day entry in **5 of 5** names. No coherent
cross-sectional edge — and the signal is rare (10–18 events per 21 years per name), so even the
absolute numbers are noisy.

## The thesis test — does the confirmation candle add edge? (harami-only placebo)

The decisive "is the third candle load-bearing?" test: keep the **down candle + inside harami
after a downtrend** event, but drop the confirming candle (enter on the bare harami). If the
confirmation candle adds edge, the confirmed entry must beat the harami-only entry.

| variant | n (pooled, H=20) | mean fwd 20d | confirmation's marginal Δ | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| confirmed three-inside-up | 64 | −106.9 bps | — | — | — |
| harami-only (no confirmation) | 211 | +91.4 bps | **−198.3 bps** | −2.49 | 0.015 |

The confirmation candle doesn't add edge — it *destroys* it. The bare harami (a far more common
event) averages **+91 bps** over 20 days; adding the "confirming" third candle drags the average to
**−107 bps**, a **−198 bps** swing that is statistically significant the *wrong* way (Welch
*t* = −2.49, *p* = 0.015). Mechanically this makes sense: requiring the third candle to close
*up* means you buy *after* a one-day pop, i.e. you chase — the confirmation candle is the worst part
of the rule, not the best. **The confirmation candle is busted as a source of edge.**

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real reversal

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* three-inside-up bounce (knob `edge`), the same confirmed
rule behaves exactly as it must — so the flat (and negative) real-tape result is a genuine
"nothing there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | confirmed | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no bounce) | 20 | −87.1 bps | 45% | −1.18 |
| **0.60** (real planted bounce) | 20 | +341.6 bps | 75% | **+4.43** |

With no planted bounce the control sits below zero with *t* ≈ −1.2 (no false positive); a real
planted reversal lights up at *t* = +4.43 with a 75% win-rate. The detector is live — when there is
a real three-inside-up edge to find, this exact rule finds it.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The confirmed three-inside-up does **not** beat a drift-matched random
  baseline (conf − random = +20.1 / −43.2 / −139.9 / −132.3 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the
  confirmed-vs-random Welch *t* never clears 2, and the rule's own one-sample *t* never clears 2
  either — it turns negative at 20 days). There isn't even a beta mirage to strip; the "reversal"
  is, on average, followed by a drop.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No residual edge — and no free drift either; costs only deepen the
  hole. The pattern is rare (64 signals in 21 years across 5 tapes) and loses to a coin-flip entry
  in every name. Nothing to scale.
- **"Does the confirmation candle add edge?" — BUSTED.** Dropping the confirming candle (the
  harami-only placebo) *improves* the 20-day return by **+198 bps** (Welch *t* = −2.49 for the
  confirmation's contribution, *p* = 0.015). The third candle — the very thing the folklore prizes
  — is the worst part of the rule: it forces you to buy after a one-day pop. The three-inside-up is
  chart-pattern theatre, not a forecasting strategy.
